title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: No SQL queries are constructed directly in this code. All database operations use Django ORM methods (Rule.objects.get(), AlertRule.objects.get(), RuleSnooze.objects.get_or_create()) with parameterized lookups. The rule_id parameter is passed to ORM methods, not concatenated into raw SQL.

The endpoint uses ProjectAlertRulePermission for authorization, but there's a potential IDOR vulnerability. After fetching the rule by rule_id (line 78 or 86), the code calls can_edit_alert_rule() to check permissions (line 91). However, there's no explicit check that the rule belongs to the project parameter. The rule could theoretically belong to a different project. The ProjectEndpoint base class may provide project validation, but without seeing that code, the authorization check appears to rely on can_edit_alert_rule() which checks organization/team membership but not project ownership.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit check that the fetched rule (issue_alert_rule or metric_alert_rule) belongs to the project parameter before proceeding. For example: `if issue_alert_rule.project_id != project.id: raise ValidationError(...)` or use Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id, project=project) to ensure project ownership at the ORM level.
